blocks.text: I told an AI to build me an entire Pokémon-style game from scratch. Not a tech demo — the whole thing. And it runs in your browser with zero dependencies.
It started with literally nothing, so it wrote its own engine. Procedural monster sprites. A chiptune synthesizer for the music. An eleven-map region to explore.
Then it built a real battle system — all seventeen types, status effects, crits, stat stages, even catching, with proper ball-shake odds.
There are four gyms, and every HM actually gates the world. Cut clears the desert. Strength moves boulders. Surf crosses the sea. Waterfall climbs into Victory Road.

And after the Elite Four, it rebuilt the one feature Nintendo abandoned a decade ago: the Dream World. Tuck a Pokémon in at the Entralink, befriend one inside a dream, and it wakes up in the Entree Forest with its hidden ability. Guaranteed catch.
So yes — an AI just resurrected a dead Pokémon feature. It's free, it runs in the browser, and the code is linked below.
